name: Blow dryer + round brush

lead: A blow dryer pushes heated air through hair while a round brush adds tension and curve, which lifts the roots and sets volume. The combination is used to create a fuller, shaped result than air-drying provides.

It is widely recommended in grooming communities for thinning and fine hair, where lift at the crown and hairline can make the hair look denser. Technique, rather than equipment price, is reported to have the largest effect.

paras: Heat evaporates water and temporarily breaks hydrogen bonds in the hair keratin. Hair cooled in a lifted or curved shape re-forms those bonds, holding the style until moisture returns.

Heat damage is the main documented concern. Studies on hair tresses report lifted and cracked cuticles at high temperatures, with damage increasing with heat and with drying very wet hair. Holding the dryer at a distance, keeping it moving, towel-drying first and using heat protectants are reported to reduce harm, and some reviews note that air-drying is not clearly safer. Results are short-term and reset with each wash.
